title: Enumerations, enum constants and underlying integer considerations
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its C rules.
Trace the example and identify data or resource flow.
Recognize relevant safety and failure cases.
Apply the concept in a tested C program.

understand.concept: An enum defines a set of named integer constant values and an enumeration type. Enumerators are integer constant expressions. The compatible integer type used for an enum is implementation-defined within the constraints of the C standard.
understand.whyItMatters: Named states are clearer than unexplained numeric codes, but programs should not assume every enum has a fixed width or external representation.
understand.analogy: Treat each object or stream as a resource with a defined lifetime and explicit rules for access.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's formal object, storage-duration, alignment or library rules.

explain.narrative:
An enum defines a set of named integer constant values and an enumeration type. Enumerators are integer constant expressions. The compatible integer type used for an enum is implementation-defined within the constraints of the C standard.

Check all allocation, I/O and conversion results. Respect object bounds and lifetime, initialize data before reading it, and define who owns and releases each resource.

hints: An enum variable can hold integer values beyond the named enumerators depending on its compatible type; validate external values.
